sources.entry: Wallabag - Wallabag, formerly Poche, is a web application allowing you to save articles to read them later with improved readability. (Source Code) MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: wallabag is a self-hostable web application for saving web pages to read later, extracting the article content so it reads without pop-ups and clutter.
summary.what_it_does: wallabag saves web pages for later reading by extracting their main content, so distractions like pop-ups are removed. It can be installed on your own server, or you can use the hosted service at wallabag.it instead. The README points to separate official apps and extensions: an Android app, an iOS app, and a browser extension (wallabagger). A GNOME app called read-it-later is listed as not maintained by the project. Content extraction relies on Graby, php-readability and ftr-site-config. Translations are handled through Weblate. The documentation lives in the doc/ directory of the repository.
use_cases: remove clutter and pop-ups from web pages
archive web articles for offline reading
how_to_run: If the default make is not GNU make, run gmake install instead
Configure a virtual host to point to your wallabag installation
notable: Official mobile apps for Android and iOS, plus a browser extension
Can be self-hosted or used through the hosted wallabag.it service
Content extraction removes distractions from saved pages
caveats: Requirements are described in the external documentation rather than the README
The GNOME read-it-later app is not maintained by this project
Install requires a web server virtual host setup
